decisions.reason: High visibility on the homepage and core email service role create strong escalation pressures from sunk costs and public commitment, leading management to persist.
The dedicated product page signals moderate investment and public commitment, making managers justify prior decisions and continue despite early disappointment.
Only a brief mention on the website indicates low sunk costs and weak public commitment, so disappointing results are less likely to trigger escalation and the product can be dropped.
As a minor feature with minimal website presence, its low investment and peripheral role reduce escalation tendencies, making it a prime candidate for removal.
Minimal visibility and an add-on security nature imply limited commitment, so managers will not escalate and are likely to cut it when results disappoint.
Like other merely mentioned products, low sunk costs and low public commitment weaken escalation of commitment, favoring discontinuation.
